status_summary: A presidential memorandum of 2025-09-09 directed the HHS Secretary to take appropriate action on transparency and accuracy in direct-to-consumer drug advertising, including more risk information where the law permits, and the FDA Commissioner to enforce the advertising provisions of the drug law, without deadlines or a stated rulemaking. The same day FDA, with HHS, announced thousands of letters to drug makers to remove misleading ads, about 100 cease-and-desist letters already issued and a rulemaking to close the adequate provision option for broadcast and digital ads. FDA's Transparency in Direct-to-Consumer Advertising rule (RIN 0910-AJ14, revising 21 CFR 202.1) is listed at the proposed rule stage in the Unified Agenda and in the HHS agenda published 2026-08-14, as economically significant and major, with a proposal targeted for December 2026. No proposed rule had been published in the Federal Register as of 2026-10-17.

timeline.event: Presidential memorandum on misleading direct-to-consumer prescription drug advertisements directs HHS and FDA to act on transparency, accuracy and enforcement.

uncertainties: GovInfo notes that an original copy of the memorandum was not available for verification. The FDA press announcement of 2025-09-09 was read on fda.gov and gives the counts of thousands of letters and about 100 cease-and-desist letters without a published list; a later law-firm report gives about 100 cease-and-desist and about 40 untitled letters, which was not checked against FDA data. Individual warning letters dated 2025-09-09 were not opened in this review. A Federal Register API search for direct-to-consumer advertising documents since 2025-08-01 found only the agenda listings and no FDA proposed or final rule. A law-firm alert titled as an FDA proposal describes only the agenda listing. The document's concern with ad placement on media outlets is not addressed by the announced actions, so alignment is partial.
